ISTJ>INTJ.title: Before deciding, you look back at how it was done last year.
ISTJ>INTJ.body: You check how things went before, then think about what comes next. You take your time thinking alone, and you decide with logic. When planning work, you look back at last year's way of doing things and think about next year too. People see you as someone good at making plans.
ISTJ>INTJ.say: "I want to think about three years from now, too."
ISTJ>INTJ.do: When you buy a phone, you pick one based on how many years it'll last.
ISTJ>INTJ.worry: You can't easily decide whether to stick with the old way or try a new one. Some days you have so much on your mind that your head never gets a break.
ISTJ>INTJ.karai: You turned down an invite because you "had plans." The plan was cleaning your room.
ISTJ>INTJ.aru: You start planning a trip and end up looking up towns you'd like to live in. Suddenly it's midnight, and you still haven't booked a place to stay.
ISTJ>INTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. That's why, once you start looking into something, you end up thinking far ahead.
ISTJ>INTJ.yure: Only one part is different: whether you go by facts and experience or by ideas. If you answer while thinking about work, you lean toward facts. If you think about the future, you lean toward ideas.
ISTJ>INTJ.plus: It takes you a while to decide because you think things through carefully. People feel safe with a plan you made.
ISTJ>INTJ.tip: Try setting a 30-minute timer before you start looking things up. When it rings, you can ask yourself, "What was I supposed to decide today?"
ISTJ>INTJ.hidden: Do you quickly notice when someone's story doesn't match what they said before? That comes from your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Before talking about big plans, check the current numbers first. People will find it easier to say yes.

ISTJ>INTP.title: Someone who wonders, "Why is it done this way?"
ISTJ>INTP.body: You follow the set steps properly. But as you go, you start wondering, "Why do we even do it this way?" You think quietly on your own and decide with logic, and that never changes. Sometimes, while looking into things, you find a better way.
ISTJ>INTP.say: "This order works, but why is it in this order?"
ISTJ>INTP.do: When buying an appliance, you compare the specs yourself before asking the staff.
ISTJ>INTP.worry: You want to follow the rules, but you also want to try another way, so you get stuck. Thinking is fun for you, so sometimes you end up rushing right before a deadline.
ISTJ>INTP.karai: In a meeting where everyone's supposed to decide together, you've already reached the answer on your own.
ISTJ>INTP.aru: You were reading the manual, and now you're watching a video about how the thing works. The day before a deadline, you somehow can't stop.
ISTJ>INTP.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone and decide with logic. You get stuck because you really like to think.
ISTJ>INTP.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. If you picture work with a deadline, your answers come out more structured. If you picture looking things up on a day off, they come out freer.
ISTJ>INTP.plus: You get stuck because you notice there might be a better way. When someone who follows the rules says, "We should fix this part," people listen.
ISTJ>INTP.tip: When a video or article catches your eye, don't watch it right away. Just leave the tab open. If you look at it after you're done, you won't panic before deadlines.
ISTJ>INTP.hidden: Even if you think you go with the flow, do you lay out everything you'll pack the night before a trip? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it at work too, and you'll see your ideas through to the end.

ISTJ>ENTJ.title: Someone who prepares well and pulls the discussion together.
ISTJ>ENTJ.body: Before a meeting, you read the materials carefully, and at the end you say, "Okay, let's do it this way." You decide with logic and stick to a plan. You often lead in front of people, but afterward you want time alone to rest.
ISTJ>ENTJ.say: "I've checked the numbers. Let's aim bigger next year."
ISTJ>ENTJ.do: You put all of next month's plans into your calendar early.
ISTJ>ENTJ.worry: Because you work hard in front of others, your alone time keeps getting pushed back. You often can't decide whether to play it safe or go for it.
ISTJ>ENTJ.karai: Even on your day off, you're planning next week in your head.
ISTJ>ENTJ.aru: At meetings you lead everyone, but at home you can't get off the couch. You decide your replies can wait until tomorrow.
ISTJ>ENTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone and trust facts and experience. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people and follow your ideas. In both your temperament and your personality, you decide with logic and stick to a plan. You get tired after a day of leading because you put in that much effort.
ISTJ>ENTJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and facts or ideas. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your meeting-day self or your day-off self.
ISTJ>ENTJ.plus: Wanting a break doesn't mean you're weak. It means you work hard every day.
ISTJ>ENTJ.tip: On days with a big meeting, decide ahead of time not to make evening plans. Then it's easier to say "Not that day" when someone invites you.
ISTJ>ENTJ.hidden: Even when talking about big plans, do you first ask, "How were last month's numbers?" That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Because of it, people think, "If it's this person, it'll be fine."

ISTJ>ENTP.title: Someone who throws out ideas, then looks into them properly.
ISTJ>ENTP.body: You seem to talk off the top of your head, but you look into things properly afterward. When you decide something, you think it through with logic. Some days you want to chat with lots of people, and some days you want to be quiet alone. Friends are sometimes surprised when you say, "I looked into what we talked about."
ISTJ>ENTP.say: "Didn't we try that before, and it didn't work?"
ISTJ>ENTP.do: When the family can't pick a trip, you line up the cost of each place and compare.
ISTJ>ENTP.worry: You come up with so many ideas that you wear yourself out trying to pick one. The gap between days you want to talk and days you don't want to see anyone is big, and it confuses even you.
ISTJ>ENTP.karai: You argue the other side on purpose, then pick the safest option in the end.
ISTJ>ENTP.aru: At a party you say, "Wouldn't it be fun to do this?" That night on the train home, you're looking up costs and dates.
ISTJ>ENTP.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people, follow your ideas, and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you decide with logic. Your mood changes from day to day because you adjust to each situation.
ISTJ>ENTP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result changes easily. Answer as your idea-sharing self and you'll get a lively, free result. Answer as your quietly-researching self and you'll get a calm, structured one.
ISTJ>ENTP.plus: You can't narrow down your ideas because you have so many. And since you check on what you said later, people trust you.
ISTJ>ENTP.tip: Decide, "If I still want to do it a week later, I'll do it." After a busy, social day, keep the next day free of plans so the tiredness doesn't stick around.
ISTJ>ENTP.hidden: When talking one-on-one, can you listen quietly until the other person is done? That's your temperament, which recharges with time alone. Value it, and friends will start saying you're easy to talk to.

ISTJ>INFJ.title: Someone who thinks it through with you when you need advice.
ISTJ>INFJ.body: When someone comes to you for advice, you first sort out what happened, then think with them about what they want. You value time alone to think, and you like to settle future plans early. You say what needs to be said, but you think hard about how to say it.
ISTJ>INFJ.say: "Okay, I get the situation. So what do you want to do?"
ISTJ>INFJ.do: You set the date and the restaurant for plans with friends a month ahead.
ISTJ>INFJ.worry: When the right thing and the kind thing are different, you can't decide which to say. You do so much for others that your own feelings get put off.
ISTJ>INFJ.karai: Somehow you're always the one sorting out dates in the group chat.
ISTJ>INFJ.aru: While listening to a friend's love problems, you're planning in your head: "First say this, then..." You go back and forth on whether to say it or keep quiet, and can't fall asleep that night.
ISTJ>INFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience and decide with logic. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas and decide with your feelings. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone and stick to a plan. You hesitate because you really care about the other person.
ISTJ>INFJ.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture work and you lean toward logic. Picture a friend asking for advice and you lean toward feelings.
ISTJ>INFJ.plus: Hesitating shows you really think about how the other person feels. You can say hard things in a way that gets through.
ISTJ>INFJ.tip: When someone asks for advice, first ask, "Do you want me to listen, or think it through with you?" Once you know what they want, you'll spend less time unsure.
ISTJ>INFJ.hidden: When a friend talks about a dream, do you want to ask, "When will you start? What do you need?" That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. With it, plans that might stay just talk actually get moving.

ISTJ>INFP.title: Someone who finishes the to-dos, then gets lost in what they love.
ISTJ>INFP.body: You get things done properly by the deadline. After that, you lose track of time doing what you love. Getting your energy back with time alone never changes for you. Watching one favorite movie after work might be the thing you look forward to.
ISTJ>INFP.say: "I've finished what you asked. I'll head home now."
ISTJ>INFP.do: On days off, you walk around your neighborhood alone, listening to your favorite songs.
ISTJ>INFP.worry: Some days "I should do this properly" and "I want to do what I like" pop up at the same time, and you end up stuck in between. When you understand something in your head but your heart doesn't follow, you blame yourself.
ISTJ>INFP.karai: The day after a fun party, you don't reply to anyone and just lie around at home.
ISTJ>INFP.aru: Every morning you get up at the same time and do chores in the same order. On a day off you think, "I'd like to see the ocean," and next thing you know you're looking up train transfers in detail.
ISTJ>INFP.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas, decide with your feelings, and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone. It's natural for "properly" and "as I like" to clash, and you don't have to give up either one.
ISTJ>INFP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your weekday self or as your self doing what you love can give totally different results.
ISTJ>INFP.plus: Days when your heart doesn't follow show that you really feel your own feelings. People who make time for what they love enjoy their days.
ISTJ>INFP.tip: Once a week, decide "this time is just for what I like" and put it in your calendar. If it's a plan, you won't feel like you're slacking while you enjoy it.
ISTJ>INFP.hidden: While listening to a friend's problem, are you thinking somewhere in your head, "The cause is probably this"? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Listen kindly first, then use it, and people will count on you to help find answers.

ISTJ>ENFJ.title: Someone who doesn't just cheer you on, but helps you prepare.
ISTJ>ENFJ.body: When you support someone, you don't stop at words. You help them prepare too. You settle future plans early and stick to them. You often stand in front of people, but you also want quiet time alone.
ISTJ>ENFJ.say: "You'll do great on tomorrow's test. I'm rooting for you."
ISTJ>ENFJ.do: For a friend's birthday party, you decide early who handles the gift and the cake.
ISTJ>ENFJ.worry: The harder you try to meet everyone's expectations, the less alone time you get. You often can't decide whether to put feelings first or stick to the rules.
ISTJ>ENFJ.karai: You praise other people a lot, but about yourself you only say, "I'm not there yet."
ISTJ>ENFJ.aru: You help a younger coworker practice a presentation and clap, "That was great!" On the way home, you message them, "They might ask about this part."
ISTJ>ENFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, and decide with logic. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people, follow your ideas, and decide with your feelings. In both your temperament and your personality, you stick to a plan. That's why you can offer both encouragement and help getting ready.
ISTJ>ENFJ.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as yourself cheering someone on or as yourself preparing alone can flip the result.
ISTJ>ENFJ.plus: You overdo it because seeing people try hard makes you truly happy. Younger people remember a senior like that for a long time.
ISTJ>ENFJ.tip: On days you help someone, tell them at the start when you'll finish. Saying "That's it for today" is also a way of caring for them.
ISTJ>ENFJ.hidden: Do good ideas come to you while reading or walking alone? That's your temperament, which recharges with time alone. Put that time in your schedule, and your energy for supporting others will last longer.

ISTJ>ENFP.title: Someone who starts on a whim and keeps it up for a long time.
ISTJ>ENFP.body: You start new things on a whim, yet somehow keep them up for a long time. In this combination, all four parts of your temperament and personality are flipped. You love having fun with people, and you're also good at quietly sticking with something on your own. You might be the only one still going to the class a friend talked you into.
ISTJ>ENFP.say: "This looks fun. Let's try it once!"
ISTJ>ENFP.do: When you find an event that looks interesting, you message a friend right away: "Want to go?"
ISTJ>ENFP.worry: New things excite you, but when changes keep coming, you suddenly get tired. Some days, after acting on impulse, you scold yourself, "I need to get it together."
ISTJ>ENFP.karai: You say "I'm in!" right away, but you already picked out your outfit the night before.
ISTJ>ENFP.aru: You tell people you started your balcony garden "just for fun." But you water it every morning without fail, and on trip days you ask your family to take over before you leave.
ISTJ>ENFP.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people, follow your ideas, decide with your feelings, and go with the flow. All four parts are flipped in this combination. That's why you can start on impulse and keep going steadily.
ISTJ>ENFP.yure: All four parts are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Answering as your day-out-with-friends self or your usual weekday self could give opposite results.
ISTJ>ENFP.plus: You look back after acting on impulse because you want to take care of what you started. Not many people can keep up the things they started on a whim.
ISTJ>ENFP.tip: When you start something new, try deciding "just two weeks to begin with." It's easy to jump in, and you can calmly decide whether to keep going.
ISTJ>ENFP.hidden: You seem to go with the flow, but when shopping, do you carefully compare prices and reviews? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Use it at work, and your ideas will sound convincing and get people moving.

ISTJ>ISTJ.title: Someone who keeps their promises.
ISTJ>ISTJ.body: Anything you're asked to do is done the day before the deadline. You check facts one by one and finish what you decide to do. You do well at a workplace with clear steps, but you tire quickly in places where everything gets decided on a whim.
ISTJ>ISTJ.say: "Let me check how it went last time, then I'll get back to you."
ISTJ>ISTJ.do: You always arrive ten minutes early to meet someone.
ISTJ>ISTJ.worry: Sudden changes of plans and unclear instructions wear you out. You wonder if something's wrong with you, but often the way things are done just doesn't suit you.
ISTJ>ISTJ.karai: When told "Just do it however," you ask, "How much is 'however'?"
ISTJ>ISTJ.aru: Before a trip, you can't relax until you've looked up even the transfer times. When someone says, "Let's decide as we go today," you get a little restless.
ISTJ>ISTJ.why: Your temperament and personality are the same combination. You recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, decide with logic, and stick to a plan, and it shows on both sides. That's why your personality tends to show up clearly in your result.
ISTJ>ISTJ.yure: Your temperament and personality match, so your result doesn't change much. Still, if you take it on a day when sudden changes have worn you out, your answers may come out a little different.
ISTJ>ISTJ.plus: Unclear things tire you out because you want to finish things properly. Thanks to your checking, the people around you make far fewer mistakes.
ISTJ>ISTJ.tip: When a conversation is vague, try asking, "So, by what time should we decide?" That alone makes a big difference in how tired you get.
ISTJ>ISTJ.hidden: On a trip, have you ever wandered into a small shop that wasn't on the plan and had a great time? Going with the moment is something you can do, too. Leave some free time now and then, and time with friends will get even more fun.

ISTJ>ISFJ.title: Someone people feel safe having around.
ISTJ>ISFJ.body: At work and at home, people say they feel safe when you're around. You get your energy back with time alone, check the facts, and stick to a plan. Your work is accurate, and when someone's busy, you quietly answer their phone for them.
ISTJ>ISFJ.say: "I've already printed the handouts for tomorrow's meeting."
ISTJ>ISFJ.do: You quietly leave a drink on the desk of a coworker who looks unwell.
ISTJ>ISFJ.worry: Even when something needs to be said, you worry it'll hurt the other person and can't say it. As you keep saying yes to favors, your own time disappears.
ISTJ>ISFJ.karai: When someone asks, "Want some help?", you end up saying, "I'm fine."
ISTJ>ISFJ.aru: You spot a mistake in a coworker's paperwork, but worry they'll feel bad if you say something, so you quietly fix it. Before you know it, you're taking other people's work home.
ISTJ>ISFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to decide with logic. Through experience, you've also learned to decide with your feelings. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, and stick to a plan. That's why, when you notice a mistake, you're unsure how to bring it up.
ISTJ>ISFJ.yure: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture work and you lean toward logic. Picture family or friends and you lean toward feelings.
ISTJ>ISFJ.plus: You can't say it because you understand how the other person feels. Someone accurate and kind is a person everyone at work can count on.
ISTJ>ISFJ.tip: When you notice a mistake, don't fix it quietly. Just say, "The date here was wrong." They'll be careful next time, and you won't end up with extra work.
ISTJ>ISFJ.hidden: When picking an appliance or a place to move, do you compare prices and convenience one by one before deciding? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Try using it when you can't decide because you're thinking too much about others' feelings.

ISTJ>ESTJ.title: Someone who prepares alone, then runs the show on the day.
ISTJ>ESTJ.body: People think, "If we leave it to them, it'll be fine." You check the facts, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. You prepare quietly on your own, and on the day you stand in front of everyone and get them moving.
ISTJ>ESTJ.say: "Three things to do today. Let's go in this order."
ISTJ>ESTJ.do: At the supermarket, you go through the aisles in the order of what you need to buy.
ISTJ>ESTJ.worry: The more people rely on you, the more often you're in front of others, and your alone time shrinks. On days you're too harsh with someone who's careless, you quietly regret it later.
ISTJ>ESTJ.karai: You tell others "Rest is part of the job," but you haven't used a single day of your own paid leave.
ISTJ>ESTJ.aru: You handle the work party well as the organizer, but once it's over you want to be alone right away, so you skip the after-party saying, "I have an early morning."
ISTJ>ESTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. That's why, after leading a group, you want to be alone.
ISTJ>ESTJ.yure: Only one part is different: getting energy from people or recharging alone. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your leading-at-work self or your day-off self.
ISTJ>ESTJ.plus: You can look back and regret it because you really pay attention to people. Leaders like that are trusted for a long time.
ISTJ>ESTJ.tip: When you schedule an event, keep the next morning free too. It also helps to decide, "I'll go to the after-party for just the first 30 minutes."
ISTJ>ESTJ.hidden: Even while running things, do you step back a little and watch how everyone's doing? Noticing who's struggling comes from your temperament, which likes to think things through alone. Use it, and you'll be a leader who notices the small things.

ISTJ>ESFJ.title: Someone who gets everything ready for a get-together.
ISTJ>ESFJ.body: When there's a get-together, you settle the date, place, and seats without missing a thing, and you remember what everyone likes. You check the facts and stick to a plan. Some days chatting with people gives you energy, and some days you want quiet time alone. At family gatherings, you end up going back and forth between the kitchen and the table.
ISTJ>ESFJ.say: "Everyone can make it on this day, so let's go with it."
ISTJ>ESFJ.do: When someone at work is off, you take their calls too.
ISTJ>ESFJ.worry: While looking after everyone, your alone time vanishes and you suddenly feel drained. You want people to follow the rules, but you don't want to blame them either, and you get stuck.
ISTJ>ESFJ.karai: When you organize, your own seat is always by the door.
ISTJ>ESFJ.aru: As organizer of a farewell party, you even ask what foods everyone dislikes. But when someone asks, "What do you want to eat?" you can't answer.
ISTJ>ESFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone and decide with logic. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people and decide with your feelings. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience and stick to a plan. That's why, even after preparing carefully, you still wonder if everyone's having fun.
ISTJ>ESFJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your party-organizer self or your quiet-day-alone self.
ISTJ>ESFJ.plus: You get stuck because you care about both the rules and people's feelings. When you're there, get-togethers run smoothly.
ISTJ>ESFJ.tip: When you're the organizer, add one dish you want to eat. You'll feel, "I'm allowed to enjoy this too," and you'll be less tired afterward.
ISTJ>ESFJ.hidden: When it's time to split the bill or decide who does what, can you decide without hesitating? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Use it, and people will think, "If they're in charge, it'll be fair."

ISTJ>ISTP.title: Someone who fixes things as soon as they break.
ISTJ>ISTP.body: When something goes wrong, you don't panic. You fix it with whatever you have on hand. You value time alone, check the facts, and think with logic. Some days you prepare ahead, and some days you figure it out on the spot. If a bike chain comes off, you crouch down and fix it right there.
ISTJ>ISTP.say: "I fixed it for now. I'll make sure it doesn't happen again."
ISTJ>ISTP.do: When a light bulb burns out, you replace it right away and buy a spare while you're at it.
ISTJ>ISTP.worry: Some days you want to stick to the plan, and some days you want to follow your mood, so it's hard to find your own pace. You don't like being tied down by rules, but you can't relax when nothing is decided.
ISTJ>ISTP.karai: You say, "I don't read manuals," but you read the troubleshooting page carefully.
ISTJ>ISTP.aru: You say, "It'll work out," yet your bag has a spare charger, bandages, and a folding umbrella.
ISTJ>ISTP.why: By birth, you're the type to stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, and decide with logic. That's why you don't just fix things, you also want to prepare for next time.
ISTJ>ISTP.yure: Only one part is different: sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture a work deadline and you answer like a planner. Picture a day off and you answer like someone who goes with the flow.
ISTJ>ISTP.plus: It's hard to find your pace because you can switch depending on the moment. Someone who fixes things on the spot and prepares for next time is a big help.
ISTJ>ISTP.tip: On days off, try planning only half the day, like "plans in the morning, nothing in the afternoon." You won't feel restless, and you can still relax.
ISTJ>ISTP.hidden: Before an exam or a move, do you naturally decide what to take care of first? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it for big goals, and you'll finish even the things you started on a whim.

ISTJ>ISFP.title: Someone who adds a bit of their own taste to the usual way.
ISTJ>ISFP.body: You do what's set properly, but you add a bit of your own taste to it. You get your energy back with time alone, and you care about what's right in front of you. Even when choosing clothes, you stick to your usual style but change the color depending on your mood.
ISTJ>ISFP.say: "It's cold today, so I'll put some ginger in the soup."
ISTJ>ISFP.do: You measure everything to follow the recipe, then taste it and change it just a little at the end.
ISTJ>ISFP.worry: Some days "I should do this properly" and "I want to go at my own pace" are both there, and you end up stuck in between. You're not good at putting your feelings into words, and it's frustrating when they don't come across.
ISTJ>ISFP.karai: Your day off was supposed to be relaxing, but it's filled with laundry and grocery runs.
ISTJ>ISFP.aru: You clean on the same days every week. You don't feel done until you open the window and put on your favorite music.
ISTJ>ISFP.why: By birth, you're the type to decide with logic and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to decide with your feelings and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone and trust facts and experience. That's why a little of your own taste always slips into the usual way.
ISTJ>ISFP.yure: Two parts are different: deciding with logic or with feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Answer thinking about work or chores and the result comes out structured. Answer thinking about your days off and it comes out softer.
ISTJ>ISFP.plus: You struggle to put feelings into words because what you feel is detailed. Often, what you do gets the message across before words do.
ISTJ>ISFP.tip: When you can't say how you feel, it's okay to say, "Let me think about it." If you give one reason a little later, even a few words will get through.
ISTJ>ISFP.hidden: When choosing furniture or appliances, do you carefully compare size and ease of use before deciding? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. When sharing your feelings, giving one reason makes them easier to understand.

ISTJ>ESTP.title: Someone who moves fast, but is already prepared.
ISTJ>ESTP.body: When something happens, you're the first to act. But behind that, you always look things up and prepare. You care about the facts in front of you and decide with logic, and that doesn't change. Even if plans change on a trip, you can quickly decide where to go next.
ISTJ>ESTP.say: "I looked up a route that works even in the rain. Let's go."
ISTJ>ESTP.do: If your bike tires are low, you pump them up before heading out.
ISTJ>ESTP.worry: The urge to move fast clashes with the urge to prepare so nothing goes wrong, and you get tired before deciding. After a lively day, you feel off if you don't get quiet time alone.
ISTJ>ESTP.karai: The person who said "Let's just try it" read the reviews carefully before starting.
ISTJ>ESTP.aru: A friend says, "Let's go out now!" and you answer, "I'm in!" right away. But your bag already has a first-aid kit in it.
ISTJ>ESTP.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience and decide with logic. You can move fast because of the preparing you always do.
ISTJ>ESTP.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your out-with-friends self or your preparing-alone self.
ISTJ>ESTP.plus: You over-prepare because you want everyone to relax and have fun. There's surely someone your preparing has helped.
ISTJ>ESTP.tip: After plans with friends, keep the next morning as alone time. Narrow what you bring to three "must-haves," and you can head out light.
ISTJ>ESTP.hidden: When you focus alone on cooking or building models, do you lose track of time? That's your temperament, which recharges with time alone. Use that focus at work, and people will see you as someone who gets it done.

ISTJ>ESFP.title: Someone who laughs a lot and still keeps an eye on the last train.
ISTJ>ESFP.body: You brighten up the room, but you keep an eye on the time and the money. So the people with you can relax and have fun. You care about what's in front of you and what you've actually tried. After a fun day, you want to take it easy alone the next day.
ISTJ>ESFP.say: "This place is so good! Let's come back again."
ISTJ>ESFP.do: When you find something tasty on a trip, you buy some for everyone.
ISTJ>ESFP.worry: The more fun you have, the more you want alone time afterward, and that surprises even you. You want to enjoy yourself fully, but you can't help thinking about what's next or about money.
ISTJ>ESFP.karai: You said, "Let's not plan anything today," but you've already booked the restaurant.
ISTJ>ESFP.aru: At karaoke, you're the most excited one. But ten minutes before the end, you've already figured out how much each person owes.
ISTJ>ESFP.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone, decide with logic, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people, decide with your feelings, and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience. That's why, even while having fun, you keep thinking about the time.
ISTJ>ESFP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your out-with-friends self or your home-alone self can give completely different results.
ISTJ>ESFP.plus: You think ahead while having fun because you want everyone to feel good until the end. It's a relief to have someone who livens things up and wraps them up too.
ISTJ>ESFP.tip: The day after fun plans, pick a time when you won't check the group chat. If you're not chasing replies, you can really rest with time alone.
ISTJ>ESFP.hidden: When friends are about to argue, do you suggest, "Okay, let's take turns like this"? That's your temperament, which decides with logic. Use it, and people will count on you when things get tough.

ISFJ>INTJ.title: Someone who thinks far ahead for the people they care about.
ISFJ>INTJ.body: You think ahead and prepare for your family and friends. You think things through alone and stick to a plan. In discussions, you speak calmly, but what you say is clear. When planning a trip, you set the order so no one gets too tired.
ISFJ>INTJ.say: "Won't that plan get tough in six months?"
ISFJ>INTJ.do: You save a little at a time, years ahead, for a trip or a new car.
ISFJ>INTJ.worry: Even when you know it's better to be direct, picturing the other person's face makes your words stop. Some days you think so much about the future that you can't enjoy the present.
ISFJ>INTJ.karai: You say, "Either is fine," but you keep talking about the place you want to go.
ISFJ>INTJ.aru: When you want to tell a family member, "You should fix that," you keep thinking about how to say it without hurting them, and it takes you a long time to bring it up.
ISFJ>INTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience and decide with your feelings. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas and decide with logic. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone and stick to a plan. That's why, even when thinking about the future, the faces of people you care about come to mind.
ISFJ>INTJ.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture work plans and you lean toward logic and ideas. Picture your family and you lean toward facts and feelings.
ISFJ>INTJ.plus: Your words stop because you don't want to hurt anyone. People trust someone who takes the time to say hard things kindly.
ISFJ>INTJ.tip: Try starting hard conversations with, "Can I say just one thing?" With a little lead-in, the other person can listen calmly.
ISFJ>INTJ.hidden: Do you remember your friends' favorite foods and things they told you before? That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Use it, and your plans will include "they'd love this."

ISFJ>INTP.title: Someone who helps people out and ends up knowing how things work.
ISFJ>INTP.body: You help people when they ask, and along the way you get to know the subject well. You get your energy back with time alone, and you dig into anything that catches your interest. When a friend asks, "How do I do this?" you can't help giving a really thorough answer.
ISFJ>INTP.say: "I looked it up, and the way it works is really interesting."
ISFJ>INTP.do: When you find an appliance you want, you read other people's reviews late into the night before buying.
ISFJ>INTP.worry: You get so absorbed in looking things up that you forget other things you had to do. You want to go along with people, but you also want to think alone, and some days that wears you out.
ISFJ>INTP.karai: When you have plans to meet people on a day off, you feel a little heavy the day before.
ISFJ>INTP.aru: You offer to fix a friend's computer, and while looking for the cause, it turns midnight. The other thing they asked you to do has completely slipped your mind.
ISFJ>INTP.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas, decide with logic, and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone. That's why something you started for someone else can turn into research you can't stop.
ISFJ>INTP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your helping-someone self or your researching-alone self can give totally different results.
ISFJ>INTP.plus: You get absorbed because you really want to know. Someone who helps others with what they've learned is someone people rely on.
ISFJ>INTP.tip: Before you start looking something up, finish one other task first. After that, you can dig in as long as you like.
ISFJ>INTP.hidden: On days with something important, do you get ready ahead of time? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can share what you've learned by the day you promised.

ISFJ>ENTJ.title: When it's time to decide, you decide clearly.
ISFJ>ENTJ.body: When something needs deciding, you decide clearly. But afterward, you make sure to check on anyone who looks tired. You make plans early and stick to them. After work, you might hand out snacks and say, "Good job today."
ISFJ>ENTJ.say: "Thanks for staying late yesterday. Thanks to you, we're on schedule."
ISFJ>ENTJ.do: At the start of the week, you decide what to do and in what order.
ISFJ>ENTJ.worry: When you keep leading people, you lose time to relax alone. Some nights, after being direct, you worry you said too much and can't sleep.
ISFJ>ENTJ.karai: You tell others "Don't overdo it," but your own schedule is packed through the weekend.
ISFJ>ENTJ.aru: In a meeting, you clearly say, "This is the direction we'll take." That night in the bath, you're wondering, "Was I too harsh?"
ISFJ>ENTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, and decide with your feelings. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people, follow your ideas, and decide with logic. In both your temperament and your personality, you stick to a plan. That's why, after deciding clearly, you worry about how everyone feels.
ISFJ>ENTJ.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your leading-at-work self or your relaxing-at-home self can change the result a lot.
ISFJ>ENTJ.plus: You worry enough to lose sleep because you don't want to hurt anyone. When someone decides when it's time to decide, everyone else can move without second-guessing.
ISFJ>ENTJ.tip: If you think you said too much, try saying just "Thanks for yesterday" the next day. That alone can make you feel a little lighter.
ISFJ>ENTJ.hidden: Can you tell someone's tired just by looking at their face? That comes from your temperament, which decides with feelings. Value it, and even when you have to be firm, your words are less likely to hurt.

ISFJ>ENTP.title: Someone who wonders, "Isn't there an easier way?"
ISFJ>ENTP.body: When you see the usual way of doing something, you wonder, "Couldn't this be easier?" In this combination, all four parts of your temperament and personality are flipped. You enjoy lively talks with people, but you also want quiet time alone. Even with chores at home, you might change the order so everyone has an easier time.
ISFJ>ENTP.say: "You do that by hand every time? It could be easier."
ISFJ>ENTP.do: When the group chat goes quiet, you send a slightly odd topic and get it going again.
ISFJ>ENTP.worry: After sharing an idea, you keep worrying, "Did I say too much?" When lively days keep coming, you suddenly want to be alone.
ISFJ>ENTP.karai: After telling a joke, you secretly check whether the other person laughed.
ISFJ>ENTP.aru: In a meeting you say, "What if we flip it around?" and surprise everyone. On the way home, you keep thinking, "Did I say too much?"
ISFJ>ENTP.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people, follow your ideas, decide with logic, and go with the flow. All four parts are flipped in this combination. That's why, after saying something new, you worry about how the other person feels.
ISFJ>ENTP.yure: All four parts are different, so your result can change a lot each time. Answering as your chatting-with-friends self or your quiet-at-home self could give opposite results.
ISFJ>ENTP.plus: You worry you said too much because you care about people. When the person with new ideas also thinks about others' feelings, everyone feels safe to speak up.
ISFJ>ENTP.tip: Before sharing an idea, try adding, "Can I say something a little odd?" The other person can get ready to listen, and you won't worry as much afterward.
ISFJ>ENTP.hidden: When someone's having a hard time, do you help without saying anything? That comes from your temperament, which decides with feelings. With it, your new ideas become "for someone," and people accept them more easily.

ISFJ>INFJ.title: Someone who thinks about a friend's future with them.
ISFJ>INFJ.body: You listen carefully to friends and think with them about what they want to do next. You get your energy back with time alone, care about people's feelings, and set plans early. After someone opens up to you, you never forget to ask, "How's it going?"
ISFJ>INFJ.say: "Let's take our time and think together about what you want to do next."
ISFJ>INFJ.do: After listening to a friend, you find a video they'd probably like and send it to them.
ISFJ>INFJ.worry: You feel other people's worries as if they were your own, and it wears you out. Some days you think so much about the future that you get anxious.
ISFJ>INFJ.karai: You want to set plans early, but on the morning of, you kind of want to stay home.
ISFJ>INFJ.aru: On days you hear a friend's worries, you can't stop thinking about them even at home. You feel down as if it were your own problem and can't sleep.
ISFJ>INFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan. That's why, when you hear a friend's story, you start worrying about their future too.
ISFJ>INFJ.yure: Only one part is different: whether you go by facts and experience or by ideas. Picture daily chores or work and you lean toward facts. Picture the future and you lean toward ideas.
ISFJ>INFJ.plus: Other people's worries tire you out because you understand how they feel. People feel relieved when someone like you listens.
ISFJ>INFJ.tip: On days you hear a friend's worries, listen to your favorite music before bed to reset. Asking "How's it going?" the next day is enough.
ISFJ>INFJ.hidden: Do you remember the little things friends told you before, or what they like? That's your temperament, which trusts facts and experience. Use it, and you can say, "You mentioned this before," which helps people feel at ease.

ISFJ>INFP.title: Someone who thinks about what suits a person and picks it for them.
ISFJ>INFP.body: You think about people and are good at picking things that suit them. You get your energy back with time alone and care about feelings. Your favorite music and movies move you a lot, and you watch them again and again. Some days you want to stick to the plan, and some days you want to follow your mood.
ISFJ>INFP.say: "This song makes me want to cry every time I hear it."
ISFJ>INFP.do: You decide on souvenirs ahead of time, but if you see something at the shop that suits someone, you buy one more.
ISFJ>INFP.worry: You prepared ahead, but right before, you want to change it: "Actually, this one's better." Your feelings move easily, and some days little things bring you down.
ISFJ>INFP.karai: Before sending a message to someone you like, you reread it about three times.
ISFJ>INFP.aru: You had a birthday present ready a month ahead, but the night before you get a sudden idea and start redoing the wrapping.
ISFJ>INFP.why: By birth, you're the type to trust facts and experience and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to follow your ideas and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone and decide with your feelings. That's why, after preparing, you sometimes want to redo things on a whim.
ISFJ>INFP.yure: Two parts are different: facts or ideas, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture daily chores and you answer in a structured way. Picture doing what you love and you answer more freely.
ISFJ>INFP.plus: You want to redo things at the last minute because you want the person to be even happier. Something chosen with that much thought stays with them.
ISFJ>INFP.tip: Decide that you won't touch the present the night before. Save any new ideas for next time.
ISFJ>INFP.hidden: Do you handle daily chores and work properly, in a set order? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can keep doing what you love little by little.

ISFJ>ENFJ.title: Someone who reaches out to everyone and leads them along.
ISFJ>ENFJ.body: You reach out to everyone and lead them in the same direction. You also notice how each person is doing. You care about feelings and make plans early. In a club or team, you might tell someone who's been skipping practice, "Come next time."
ISFJ>ENFJ.say: "You looked worn out yesterday. Are you okay now?"
ISFJ>ENFJ.do: When no one replies to someone's post in the group chat, you send a sticker right away.
ISFJ>ENFJ.worry: While looking after everyone, you don't notice you're tired. When you're in front of people day after day, you start wanting to be alone.
ISFJ>ENFJ.karai: You're quick to carry other people's bags, but your own bag is the heaviest.
ISFJ>ENFJ.aru: After saying at your club, "Let's set a goal together!" you contact each person who couldn't come. Only after you're done do you notice you're exhausted.
ISFJ>ENFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone and trust facts and experience. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people and follow your ideas. In both your temperament and your personality, you decide with your feelings and stick to a plan. That's why, even while leading everyone, you still think about each person.
ISFJ>ENFJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and facts or ideas. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your with-the-group self or your alone-at-home self.
ISFJ>ENFJ.plus: You don't notice your own tiredness because you're paying so much attention to others. With someone like you in charge, everyone feels safe following along.
ISFJ>ENFJ.tip: After you finish contacting everyone, put your phone down and rest for the next hour. You'll notice your own tiredness more easily.
ISFJ>ENFJ.hidden: Do you feel relieved reading a favorite book or tidying your room alone? That's your temperament, which recharges with time alone. Value that time, and you can keep looking after everyone for longer.

ISFJ>ENFP.title: Someone who invites everyone and makes sure no one's left out.
ISFJ>ENFP.body: When you find something fun, you invite everyone right away. Once you've invited people, you make sure no one ends up alone. Caring about people's feelings never changes for you. At a barbecue, you might casually sit next to someone who's having trouble joining the conversation.
ISFJ>ENFP.say: "That sounds fun! I want to try it too."
ISFJ>ENFP.do: When you and a friend decide to start a new hobby, you set the next meet-up date right there.
ISFJ>ENFP.worry: After a lively time, you suddenly want to be alone and turn down invites. Sometimes after acting on a whim, you worry, "I should've prepared better."
ISFJ>ENFP.karai: You invited people "just because," but you're the one who prepared the most.
ISFJ>ENFP.aru: You love asking, "Want to have a picnic sometime?" But the week after a fun day, you want to stay in.
ISFJ>ENFP.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people, follow your ideas, and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you decide with your feelings. That's why you want to have fun together, but you also want time alone.
ISFJ>ENFP.yure: Three of the four parts are different, so your result can change a lot. Answering as your out-with-friends self or your relaxing-at-home self can give completely different results.
ISFJ>ENFP.plus: You turn down invites because you use a lot of energy when having fun. Once you feel better, you can be the one to invite people again.
ISFJ>ENFP.tip: When you make fun plans, keep the next day empty. When your rest day is already set, you can enjoy yourself fully.
ISFJ>ENFP.hidden: After inviting people, do you double-check the meeting place and time? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and even get-togethers you started on a whim can keep going.

ISFJ>ISTJ.title: Someone who follows the rules and helps people in trouble.
ISFJ>ISTJ.body: You follow rules and the usual way of doing things carefully. You get your energy back with time alone, check the facts, and stick to a plan. At work, if there's a mistake, you say so clearly. But when you see someone in trouble, you can't just leave them be.
ISFJ>ISTJ.say: "I made the format match last time."
ISFJ>ISTJ.do: You compare each month's electric bill with the same month last year.
ISFJ>ISTJ.worry: After pointing something out, you worry you hurt the other person. Some days you can't decide whether to follow the rules or help the person in front of you.
ISFJ>ISTJ.karai: You spot the wrong date on someone's paperwork before they do.
ISFJ>ISTJ.aru: You can properly speak up to someone who missed a deadline. But that night you worry, "Did I say too much?" and the next morning you go check on them.
ISFJ>ISTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to decide with your feelings. Through experience, you've also learned to decide with logic. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, and stick to a plan. That's why, after speaking up clearly, you worry about how the other person is doing.
ISFJ>ISTJ.yure: Only one part is different: deciding with logic or with feelings. Picture work and you lean toward logic. Picture family or friends and you lean toward feelings.
ISFJ>ISTJ.plus: You worry after pointing things out because you really think about the other person. Everyone trusts someone who's careful and kind.
ISFJ>ISTJ.tip: After pointing something out, add, "You're always a big help." It's easier for them to take, and you won't worry so much at night.
ISFJ>ISTJ.hidden: When someone's feeling down, do you notice right away and talk to them? That's your temperament, which decides with feelings. Use it, and even when pointing something out, you can say it in a way that gets through.

ISFJ>ISFJ.title: Someone who's always supporting the people around them.
ISFJ>ISFJ.body: You prepare ahead so the people around you don't run into trouble. You get your energy back with time alone and care about people's feelings. You feel calm when things follow the usual routine. At work, you might refill the copy paper before it runs out.
ISFJ>ISFJ.say: "Aren't you cold? Want to borrow my jacket?"
ISFJ>ISFJ.do: When someone in your family catches a cold, you have rice porridge and a sports drink ready before they ask.
ISFJ>ISFJ.worry: You can't say no when asked, so your own time disappears. Doing things for others becomes so normal that some days you lose track of how you feel.
ISFJ>ISFJ.karai: You remember your friends' birthdays, but forget your own until someone mentions it.
ISFJ>ISFJ.aru: "Want me to do that?" is your catchphrase, and before you know it your week is full of favors.
ISFJ>ISFJ.why: Your temperament and personality are the same combination. You recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan, and it shows on both sides. That's why your kindness tends to show up just as it is in your result.
ISFJ>ISFJ.yure: Your temperament and personality match, so your result doesn't change much. Still, if you take it on a day when favors have piled up and worn you out, your answers may come out a little different.
ISFJ>ISFJ.plus: You can't say no because you picture the other person's troubled face. Thanks to your support, the days of the people around you run smoothly.
ISFJ>ISFJ.tip: When someone asks a favor, don't answer right away. Try saying, "Let me check my schedule." A little time makes it easier to say no when it's too much.
ISFJ>ISFJ.hidden: Do you sometimes want to head out without any plan? Going with the moment is something you can do, too. Make a day with no plans now and then, and you'll feel lighter.

ISFJ>ESTJ.title: Someone who loves looking after people and runs things smoothly.
ISFJ>ESTJ.body: You're good at moving things along and deciding everyone's roles. But you also remember each person's situation. You check the facts and stick to a plan. For a neighborhood event, you might quietly lighten the load for people who can't come.
ISFJ>ESTJ.say: "If you have little kids, helping in the morning only is totally fine."
ISFJ>ESTJ.do: You gather the family's schedule in a calendar app and send it to everyone every week.
ISFJ>ESTJ.worry: After deciding things quickly, you worry you seemed harsh. When you're in front of people day after day, you want time to relax alone.
ISFJ>ESTJ.karai: You tell everyone, "Go home early," and you're always the one turning off the lights at the end.
ISFJ>ESTJ.aru: You run the meeting smoothly and settle the roles fast. But on the way home you worry, "Did I come off as harsh?" and send a message: "Let me know if anything comes up."
ISFJ>ESTJ.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone and decide with your feelings. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people and decide with logic. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience and stick to a plan. That's why, after deciding quickly, you worry about how the other person feels.
ISFJ>ESTJ.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and deciding with logic or with feelings. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your in-charge self or your alone-at-home self.
ISFJ>ESTJ.plus: You feel uneasy because you remember each person's situation. Since you decide with even the people who can't come in mind, everyone can take part without strain.
ISFJ>ESTJ.tip: When you assign roles, ask right then, "Tell me if anything's too much." Then you won't need to send a worried message later.
ISFJ>ESTJ.hidden: Do you feel relieved drinking your favorite tea alone? That's your temperament, which recharges with time alone. Make that time on busy nights, and you'll move smoothly the next day too.

ISFJ>ESFJ.title: At get-togethers, you make sure to talk to each person.
ISFJ>ESFJ.body: At get-togethers, you talk to each person who comes. You care about feelings, check the facts, and prepare according to plan. You like talking with people, but afterward you want time alone to rest. At a family New Year's gathering, you might even have the envelopes for the kids' gift money ready.
ISFJ>ESFJ.do: When you run into a neighbor, you remember how their family is doing and ask about them.
ISFJ>ESFJ.worry: After giving it your all at a get-together, you suddenly feel drained and don't want to talk to anyone. Some days you're so busy looking after everyone that you don't enjoy yourself.
ISFJ>ESFJ.karai: You take lots of photos of everyone, but there are hardly any of you.
ISFJ>ESFJ.aru: You agree to organize a reunion and handle both the front desk and the photos on the day. But the next week, you can't bring yourself to reply to friends' invites.
ISFJ>ESFJ.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan. That's why you want to be alone after a get-together.
ISFJ>ESFJ.yure: Only one part is different: getting energy from people or recharging alone. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your organizer self or your relaxing-at-home self.
ISFJ>ESFJ.plus: You can't reply the next week because you gave it your all on the day. When you talk to each person, people want to come again.
ISFJ>ESFJ.tip: Make the day after a get-together a day you don't have to reply to anyone. If you send a quick "I'll reply tomorrow," you can rest easy.
ISFJ>ESFJ.hidden: Do you feel calm walking alone or listening to your favorite music? That's your temperament, which recharges with time alone. Put that time on your schedule, and you'll keep your energy longer around people.

ISFJ>ISTP.title: For you, quietly helping is easier than talking.
ISFJ>ISTP.body: You'd rather help by doing something than cheer people on with words. You get your energy back with time alone and care about what's in front of you. When a family member's phone settings are off, you quietly fix them.
ISFJ>ISTP.say: "It's faster to just try it than read the manual."
ISFJ>ISTP.do: When new furniture arrives, you put it together alone that same day.
ISFJ>ISTP.worry: When someone says "Thank you," you don't know what to say back. When all you can do is listen, you can't help with your hands, and you get restless.
ISFJ>ISTP.karai: You're quick to help with other people's problems, but you never tell anyone about your own.
ISFJ>ISTP.aru: When a friend's bike chain comes off, you crouch down and fix it without a word. When they say "Thanks," you just say, "It's nothing."
ISFJ>ISTP.why: By birth, you're the type to decide with your feelings and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to decide with logic and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone and trust facts and experience. That's why your hands move before your words do.
ISFJ>ISTP.yure: Two parts are different: deciding with logic or with feelings, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Answer thinking about fixing something and you lean toward logic and the moment. Think about your family and you lean toward feelings and planning.
ISFJ>ISTP.plus: You get shy because you're not helping to be thanked. Feeling restless just means you really want to be useful to them.
ISFJ>ISTP.tip: When someone thanks you, a smile is enough. When you're just listening, find one thing you can do with your hands, like making them some tea.
ISFJ>ISTP.hidden: Do you prepare gifts ahead of time for the birthdays of people you care about? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, you don't just help in the moment, you can also prepare ahead.

ISFJ>ISFP.title: Someone who suddenly wants to take a detour on the usual route.
ISFJ>ISFP.body: You handle daily things properly, but sometimes you want to take a little detour on a whim. You get your energy back with time alone and care about people's feelings and the small things in front of you. When the season changes, you might want to swap your cushion covers.
ISFJ>ISFP.say: "Just the smell of this bakery makes me happy."
ISFJ>ISFP.do: On days off, you buy a single flower you like and put it in your room.
ISFJ>ISFP.worry: Some days you want to follow the plan, and some days you want to follow your mood, and you can't decide. Sometimes, after acting on a whim, you have small regrets.
ISFJ>ISFP.karai: When you find clothes you love, you own them in several colors.
ISFJ>ISFP.aru: Even on a day that's going to plan, if the weather's nice, you want to take a detour. But afterward, being off-schedule bugs you and you feel a little restless.
ISFJ>ISFP.why: By birth, you're the type to stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you recharge with time alone, trust facts and experience, and decide with your feelings. That's why, even on a planned day, you want to take a detour.
ISFJ>ISFP.yure: Only one part is different: sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Picture work or chores and you answer like a planner. Picture a day off and you answer like someone who goes with the flow.
ISFJ>ISFP.plus: You feel restless after a detour because you really take care of your days. Someone who finds small joys brightens up the people around them too.
ISFJ>ISFP.tip: Put 30 minutes of "detour time" into your plans. Then you can enjoy a detour without it bugging you.
ISFJ>ISFP.hidden: Before a trip, do you naturally decide what to bring and the order you'll go in? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Use it, and you can actually do the things you want to try.

ISFJ>ESTP.title: Someone who jumps in right away when someone needs help.
ISFJ>ESTP.body: When you see someone in trouble, your body moves before you think. Caring about what's right in front of you and what you've learned by doing has never changed for you. If someone drops their things on the street, you're there picking them up before anyone else.
ISFJ>ESTP.do: At a sale, when you find something you want, you try it on right there and buy it without hesitating.
ISFJ>ESTP.worry: Some days you wonder afterward whether a quick decision was the right one. Sometimes you help so eagerly that you later think, "Did I overdo it?"
ISFJ>ESTP.karai: You say, "I'm not tired," then you're the first one asleep on the train home.
ISFJ>ESTP.aru: When you help someone move, you're the first to carry the heavy boxes. But back home, you worry, "Did I overstep?"
ISFJ>ESTP.why: Caring about facts and experience is the same in your temperament and your type. Three things are different. By nature you calm down alone, decide with your feelings, and stick to a plan. Along the way, you grew into getting energy from moving with people, deciding quickly with logic, and going with the moment. So after you act fast, you look back on it alone.
ISFJ>ESTP.yure: Three things differ between your temperament and your type, so your result can change a lot. Answer as yourself on the move and you'll get an active type. Answer as yourself having a slow talk with someone close and you'll get a quieter type.
ISFJ>ESTP.plus: You think about it afterward because you care how others feel. Someone who moves right away and also cares is someone people count on.
ISFJ>ESTP.tip: When you take something on, first say, "I'll do up to here," then get moving. On nights after a busy day, take some time alone to rest.
ISFJ>ESTP.hidden: By nature, you're good at getting ready ahead of time. Before a trip, don't you quietly check the departure time and what to bring? Share it with everyone, and fewer people will be rushing on the day.

ISFJ>ESFP.title: Someone who notices the person sitting alone in a lively crowd.
ISFJ>ESFP.body: You love lively places and laugh a lot with everyone. When someone's sitting alone, you notice right away and go talk to them. You care about people's feelings and what's in front of you. At a fireworks show, you might find a spot where everyone can see well before anyone asks.
ISFJ>ESFP.say: "Isn't it cold over there? I have a lap blanket."
ISFJ>ESFP.do: When you go out, your bag always has bandages, stomach medicine, and snacks.
ISFJ>ESFP.worry: After a fun time, you suddenly feel drained and don't want to talk to anyone. After getting excited, you worry about what people thought of you.
ISFJ>ESFP.karai: You laughed and had the most fun, then at home you worry, "Was I too loud?"
ISFJ>ESFP.aru: At parties you get everyone going, but the moment you're in the taxi home, you're so drained you can't say a word.
ISFJ>ESFP.why: By birth, you're the type to recharge with time alone and stick to a plan. Through experience, you've also learned to get energy from being with people and go with the flow. In both your temperament and your personality, you trust facts and experience and decide with your feelings. That's why you feel wiped out after a fun time.
ISFJ>ESFP.yure: Two parts are different: getting energy from people or recharging alone, and sticking to a plan or going with the flow. Your result can change depending on whether you answer as your out-with-friends self or your quiet-at-home self.
ISFJ>ESFP.plus: You worry "Was I too loud?" because you think about others' feelings. Because you reach out, fewer people end up alone.
ISFJ>ESFP.tip: After fun plans, decide you don't have to force conversation on the way home. If you say, "I'm a bit tired, so I'll be quiet," everyone will understand.
ISFJ>ESFP.hidden: Before going out, do you settle what to bring and when to head home? That's your temperament, which likes to stick to a plan. Because of it, even fun days feel safe.
